requirement: Describe the AMC trial as a prospective multicenter two-arm randomized comparison of Ahmed glaucoma valve implantation with adjunctive intraoperative and postoperative mitomycin-C versus balanced-salt-solution sham, with participant-level randomization and one enrolled study eye per participant.

evidence.text: The Manual of Operation describes the multicenter randomized two-arm trial, first eligible study eye, stratified allocation, and MMC versus BSS procedures.
The SAP describes the prospective two-arm randomized AGV comparison and the two treatment regimens.

requirement: Reconcile masking before finalization: the protocol specifies participant and examination-technician masking with surgeons and local coordinators unmasked, whereas the SAP calls the study double-masked and states that participating surgeons and participants are masked.
acceptable_values: SAP masking statement corrected or justified

evidence.text: The protocol calls the trial single-masked and states that participants and technicians are masked but surgeons and local coordinators are not.
The SAP calls the trial double-masked and states that participating surgeons and study participants will be masked.

requirement: Specify equal allocation using computer-generated randomly permuted blocks of sizes 2 through 6, stratified within clinic center by primary glaucoma, secondary non-neovascular glaucoma, and neovascular glaucoma.

evidence.text: The protocol defines center-by-glaucoma-type strata, equal allocation and computer-generated varied blocks of size 2 to 6.
The SAP confirms stratification into the three glaucoma groups before randomization.

requirement: State the prospective target as 100 participants, 50 per arm, powered at at least 80% to detect a 2-mmHg between-group IOP difference with standard deviation 3 mmHg, two-sided alpha 0.05 and 15% loss to follow-up; do not substitute the registry actual enrollment of 119.

evidence.text: The protocol prospectively defines a 100-patient randomization with equal treatment allocation.
The SAP gives 50 per arm, at least 80% power, a 2-mmHg effect, SD 3 mmHg, two-tailed alpha 0.05 and 15% loss to follow-up.

requirement: Use the enrolled participant's first eligible implanted eye as the study eye and preserve one eye per participant as the efficacy and ocular-safety analysis unit.

evidence.text: For patients with two eligible eyes, only the first eligible eye to be implanted is enrolled.

requirement: Define the intention-to-treat population to retain every randomized participant in the assigned treatment arm after randomization, irrespective of subsequent treatment adherence, and bind the primary treatment comparison to that population unless adjudicated otherwise.

evidence.text: The protocol states that once randomized, participants remain in the intention-to-treat analysis.

requirement: Resolve the governing primary IOP timepoint before finalization: protocol physical page 7 labels postoperative month 6 as primary, while SAP physical pages 2-3 label month 12 as primary; do not analyze both as co-primary without an explicit decision.

evidence.text: The Manual of Operation states that the primary outcome is IOP at postoperative 6 months.
The SAP states that the primary IOP outcome and primary statistical analysis occur at 12 months.

requirement: Derive study-eye IOP from two consecutive readings as their average when they differ by no more than 1 mmHg; when they differ by more than 1 mmHg, obtain a third reading and use the median of all three, while keeping follow-up measurement time of day similar where possible.
acceptable_values: average if difference at most 1 mmHg
third reading if difference greater than 1 mmHg

evidence.text: The protocol defines the two-reading average, third-reading trigger, median rule and time-of-day precaution for IOP.

requirement: Analyze the adjudicated primary-timepoint IOP between MMC and sham arms using linear regression that accounts for the stratified randomization, and report the adjusted treatment contrast with uncertainty.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies linear regression for primary IOP while considering the stratified randomization.

notes: The source names the model but does not define exact stratum coding or effect-estimate presentation; these details require review.

requirement: Complete the primary IOP estimand by specifying the analysis population, handling of reoperation, implant removal, oral medication, missed visits and treatment discontinuation, and the population-level summary; do not silently use available cases.

evidence.text: The protocol mentions ITT and defines several failure events but does not state how those events enter the continuous IOP estimand.
The SAP specifies linear regression for IOP but does not complete the estimand or intercurrent-event strategy.

requirement: Use two-sided testing at alpha 0.05 for the primary IOP comparison and report the corresponding 95% confidence interval.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies two-sided analysis at alpha 0.05 for primary IOP.

requirement: Define treatment failure at 12 months as any of: IOP above 21 mmHg or less than 20% reduction from baseline, IOP at most 5 mmHg with at least two-line best-corrected visual-acuity loss, oral antihypertensive medication, loss of light perception, glaucoma reoperation, or implant removal.
acceptable_values: IOP above 21 mmHg or reduction below 20%
IOP at most 5 mmHg plus at least two-line BCVA loss

evidence.text: The protocol enumerates the six-part 12-month failure definition.
The SAP repeats the failure definition and classifies nonfailures with and without supplemental topical therapy.

requirement: Classify a nonfailed study eye without supplemental topical glaucoma medication as a complete success and a nonfailed eye requiring supplemental topical medication as a qualified success; repeat secondary failure analyses using 18- and 15-mmHg IOP cutoffs while retaining all other failure criteria.
acceptable_values: complete success without supplemental topical therapy
qualified success with supplemental topical therapy

evidence.text: The protocol defines complete and qualified success and the two alternative IOP thresholds.

requirement: Prespecify an executable method for binary success and time to failure, including time origin, censoring rules, effect measures and confidence intervals; the reference's generic instruction to analyze these outcomes is insufficient by itself.

evidence.text: The SAP lists binary success and time to failure as secondary analyses without specifying their executable models or censoring rules.

requirement: Define hypertensive phase as IOP above 21 mmHg during the first six postoperative months and compare its occurrence between treatment arms using logistic regression adjusted for the randomized strata.

evidence.text: The protocol defines hypertensive phase as IOP above 21 mmHg in the first six months.
The SAP specifies stratum-adjusted logistic regression for hypertensive phase.

requirement: Compare participants or study eyes with intraoperative and postoperative complications between arms using stratum-adjusted logistic regression and provide complication-specific tabulations, while distinguishing incidence from recurrent event counts.

evidence.text: The protocol requires complications to be listed and defines adverse-event collection and management.
The SAP specifies logistic regression for complications and tabulation of each complication.

requirement: Specify how missing primary-timepoint IOP, early withdrawal, missed visits, reoperation and implant removal are handled in the ITT primary analysis, with at least one sensitivity analysis targeting departures from the primary assumption.

evidence.text: The protocol states ITT retention and discusses early discontinuation but gives no primary missing-outcome method.
The SAP's statistical considerations do not define missing-data handling or sensitivity analysis.

requirement: State whether and how multiplicity is controlled across the primary IOP comparison, success, alternative IOP thresholds, hypertensive phase, visual acuity, medication use, corneal measures and complications, and label unadjusted secondary analyses as exploratory.

evidence.text: The SAP lists many outcome comparisons but provides no multiplicity strategy.

requirement: Describe the independent safety review after 30% of participants complete the six-month visit and document the reviewed safety/failure summaries and any ethical stopping recommendation; do not invent a formal efficacy boundary absent from the source.

evidence.text: The protocol assigns the SDMC an interim safety review after 30% complete six months and permits an ethical halt for extreme benefit or risk, without a numerical boundary.

requirement: Define how clinic center and the three glaucoma strata enter each adjusted model, including handling of sparse site-by-stratum cells, without substituting a post hoc pooled-site rule.

evidence.text: The protocol randomizes within center and three glaucoma categories across multiple sites.
The SAP says models adjust for the stratified design but does not define center or sparse-stratum coding.

requirement: Analyze central endothelial cell density and central corneal thickness at six and twelve months between arms using linear regression adjusted for the randomized strata, reporting baseline and follow-up summaries and treatment contrasts.

evidence.text: The protocol schedules pachymetry and specular microscopy at baseline, six and twelve months.
The SAP specifies stratum-adjusted linear regression for ECD and pachymetry differences at six and twelve months.

requirement: Anchor postoperative analyses to surgery and preserve scheduled day 1, week 1, and months 1, 2, 3, 6 and 12 visits, with explicit visit-window and unscheduled-visit rules added before implementation.

evidence.text: The protocol defines surgery as study entry, lists all scheduled postoperative visits and permits clinically required unscheduled visits.
